reason: Holds, and the correction is right. The archive.org full-text index returns the We Are Going scan (wearegoing0000kath, Jacaranda 1964) reading 'Look up, my people, / The dawn is breaking, / The world is waking / To a new bright day, / When none defame us, / No restriction tame us, / Nor colour shame us, / Nor sneer dismay.' It has no comma after waking and a full stop after dismay, then 'Now brood no more' opens stanza two. My People (1990), Gibbs' The Aborigines and the TLS review of 10 September 1964 all read new bright day. The 'bright new day' variant is the earlier magazine text (Freedomways, Winter 1963), which also lacks the colour line. So the web versions follow the magazine, not a later reprint as the note says. That is a small inaccuracy in the note, not in the line. shipped.js is clean: Oodgeroo 0 of 3, not banned. It is the poem's opening, and it is hope at dawn, which is publishable. The source is 86 characters. Since the book appeared under the name Kath Walker, the betterCitation keeps that name in parentheses so the edition can be found.
betterCitation: Oodgeroo Noonuccal, A Song of Hope, lines 1 to 8, We Are Going (Jacaranda Press, 1964, as Kath Walker)
